ledger.note: 8 June 1815: the German Confederation is founded. 'The Confederation was established by the 9th Act of the Congress of Vienna on 8 June 1815'; 'Thirty-nine states participated in the Confederation's June 1815 founding'; infobox 'Constitution adopted: 8 June 1815'. Region is the researcher's reading of the membership, without Baden and Württemberg who joined later in 1815. Repair run: the region now includes the Austrian lands the page lists (Carniola, the Littoral except Istria) and the Belgian province of Luxembourg.

1839: 'the larger province of Luxembourg had left the Confederation at its accession to Belgium in 1839' (German Confederation page; no month given). The smaller part stays the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, still a member; today's Belgian province of Luxembourg stands for the lost part. The Duchy of Limburg, 'created' in 1839 'as compensation to the Netherlands for the loss of part of its province of Luxemburg', joins on 5 September 1839 (next entry).
5 September 1839: the Duchy of Limburg joins the Confederation. 'the Duchy of Limburg was created and joined on 5 September 1839.'

region.text: East and West Prussia and much of Posen

ledger.note: 11 April 1848: East and West Prussia and much of Posen are admitted to the Confederation. 'East and West Prussia and much of Posen were admitted on 11 April 1848'; the Frankfurt Parliament had opened on 18 May 1848 (page: 'The Province of Prussia and the Grand Duchy of Posen were only included from 1848 to 1851').

19 April 1848: Prussian troops cross into Schleswig for the Confederation's federal war. 'Prussian troops crossed the Dannevirke into Schleswig on 19 April 1848'; on 12 April the Diet 'recognized the Schleswig provisional government and assigned Prussia to enforce its decrees'. The German Confederation page: 'the Confederation's only federal war'. Danes won at Bov on 9 April.

region.text: the Duchies of Auschwitz and Zator, Austrian Galicia

ledger.note: 1850: 'the Duchies of Auschwitz and Zator, parts of the Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria, were only included from 1818 to 1850.' (German Confederation page; no month). Closes the 1818 inclusion.

region.text: East and West Prussia and Posen

ledger.note: 30 May 1851: the restored Diet removes East and West Prussia and Posen. 'the restored Diet removed them on 30 May 1851'; the Confederation was 'fully reinstalled in summer 1851' after being revived in 1850 on Austrian initiative.

8 May 1852: the second London Protocol ends the First Schleswig War. Infobox '24 March 1848 - 8 May 1852', result 'Status quo ante bellum'; 'The Treaty of Berlin (2 July 1850) made peace between Prussia and Denmark' and 'the fighting continued afterwards' (Idstedt, 24-25 July 1850). The Danish dossier has Denmark regain Holstein in April 1851.

24 December 1863: 'Saxon and Hanoverian troops marched into Holstein on behalf of the Confederation' (the federal execution, Bundesexekution; Second Schleswig War page). German Confederation page: 'In 1863, the Confederation ordered the execution of the duke of Holstein (the Danish king).' Neither page says Lauenburg was occupied. Mirrors duchy-of-holstein/ledger/9 (1863-12).

The Second Schleswig War page does not say when the federal execution ended. Set to the Treaty of Vienna of 30 October 1864 ('Denmark ceded Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg to Prussia and Austria'), matching duchy-of-holstein/ledger/11 (1864-10, confidence 1); a bridge over a silence.

region.text: Hanover, Saxony and the Electorate of Hesse

ledger.note: 15 June 1866: Prussia invades Hanover, Saxony and the Electorate of Hesse. 'The Prussian Army invaded Hanover, Saxony and the Electorate of Hesse on 15 June'; the Diet had voted 'for a partial mobilization against Prussia on 14 June'.

region.text: Hanover, Saxony and the Electorate of Hesse

ledger.note: 23 August 1866: the Peace of Prague. 'The Peace of Prague on 23 August 1866 resulted in the dissolution of the German Confederation.' The infobox gives the war as '14 June - 22 July 1866'; Königgrätz was on 3 July.

union.text: Carniola and the Slovene parts of the Austrian lands: Slovenia without Prekmurje (Pomurska) and the Istrian coast ('the Littoral except Istria')
the Littoral: Gorizia
the Littoral: Trieste
South Tyrol, inside the boundaries per the page's Italy section
Trentino, inside the boundaries per the page's Italy section
Farther Pomerania east of Koszalin: Słupsk, Lębork, Bytów

region.text: all the members: the member territory as an association outline, not a state to colour: Germany without Schleswig (Holstein and Lauenburg were members), Prussia's Silesia, Neumark and Pomerania now in Poland (with Farther Pomerania east to Słupsk, Lębork and Bytów), Czechia (the Lands of the Bohemian Crown), Austria, Slovenia without Prekmurje and the Istrian coast, Gorizia and Trieste (the page's 'Austrian lands – Austria, Carinthia, Carniola and the Littoral except Istria'), Trentino-South Tyrol (the page's Italy section lists it inside the boundaries; its table footnote says upper Italian lands apart from Trieste were not included and the page does not reconcile the two), Luxembourg and Liechtenstein; Prussia's East and West Prussia and Posen are out until 1848-1851; Limburg

ledger.note: 23 August 1866: the German Confederation is dissolved. 'Under the Peace of Prague on 23 August 1866, Austria accepted the Confederation's dissolution. The remaining states confirmed it the next day.' Prussia annexed Hanover on 20 September 1866; the North German Confederation Treaty is dated 18 August 1866. Repair run: the region now includes the Austrian lands the page lists.

wars.name: First Schleswig War
wars.outcome: Danish victory, 'Status quo ante bellum' (infobox 24 March 1848 - 8 May 1852); the Confederation's only federal war (Bundeskrieg).
wars.note: The page is inconsistent on the 1849 renewal (February or 3 April 1849). Prussian forces pushed into Jutland in 1849 but the page describes no sustained occupation. The Confederation's Diet recognised the Schleswig-Holstein provisional government on 22 April 1848 (German Confederation page).

wars.name: Second Schleswig War
wars.outcome: The Confederation 'took no part, as Schleswig was not a member'; it had ordered federal execution against Holstein in 1863 and Austria and Prussia then declared war on Denmark. Denmark ceded Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg in 1864 (kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940's dossier, Treaty of Vienna 30 October 1864; that page was not opened here).
wars.note: kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940 names german-confederation as its counterpart for the 1864 contests; by this page the belligerents were Austria and Prussia, so the counterpart there should be austrian-empire and kingdom-of-prussia. Repair run: the Confederation's federal execution in Holstein (24 December 1863) is now a ledger occupation (Second Schleswig War page).

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War

zones.text: Hanover, Saxony and the Electorate of Hesse, invaded on 15 June 1866

wars.outcome: Prussian victory: 'Dissolution of the German Confederation', exclusion of Austria from German affairs; Prussia annexed Hanover, Holstein, Schleswig, Hesse-Kassel, Nassau and Frankfurt (infobox).
wars.note: Infobox '14 June - 22 July 1866'; Peace of Prague 23 August 1866. 'Most of the southern German states sided with Austria'; 'Except for Saxony, the other German states allied to Austria played little role in the main campaign.' Hanover surrendered after Langensalza.

certainty.note: Membership followed crown-land and state boundaries fixed by the Final Act and the Federal Act; no territory of its own. The outlines are an association overlay, not a colour (umbrella).

notes: Written from five pages (budget up to 5). THE CLIOPATRIA ROW IS NOT THE CONFEDERATION. Its shapes are Prussia's provinces: 1820-1865 outlines contain none of Austria or Bavaria and at most 5 cells of Baden-Württemberg (probed against the gazetteer) but all of East Prussia, West Prussia, Posen and Silesia, which 'were only included from 1848 to 1851'; the 1815-1819 outline adds Saxony and Hanover cells, the 1864 outline Prussia's Schleswig-Holstein gains, the 1866 outline the annexations of 1866 and a block of Bohemia. kingdom-of-prussia (eu-09) already uses these shapes as Prussia's land for 1815-1866, because Cliopatria's own Kingdom of Prussia row has shapes only for 1815-1847 and 1863, and asks that this dossier not paint the same cells. All eleven shapes are therefore verdict wrong here. The corrections give the Confederation's membership outline instead, built from modern countries and Polish voivodeships; it is approximate (Prussian Rhineland and Westphalia are inside Germany; see the repair run below for the Austrian lands) and, as an umbrella, must not be coloured as territory. type is umbrella (rule 4: associations are never territory); its members (kingdom-of-bavaria, kingdom-of-saxony, grand-duchy-of-baden, kingdom-of-wurttemberg, free-city-of-frankfurt, and the rest of the eu-20 list) carry the land. Events not given: the Federal Convention was dissolved on 12 July 1848 and 'fully reinstalled in summer 1851' (revived 1850): the Confederation is shown as continuous. Federal execution against Holstein (1863): see the repair run below. Hanover's annexation (20 September 1866) falls after the dissolution. The Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg partition (1826), Anhalt-Köthen (1847, merged 1853) and Hohenzollern (1850) are member-state changes inside the membership outline. Disagreements: the Austro-Prussian War page gives 14 June - 22 July 1866 in its infobox and the Peace of Prague on 23 August; the page does not date the Diet's vote as federal execution. The Danish dossier names german-confederation as the 1864 counterpart (see the Second Schleswig War entry). Gazetteer names needed: none besides the regions used (all resolve). Counterpart without a dossier: landgraviate-of-hesse-homburg (member 1817-1866, 'Hesse-Homburg joined on 7 July 1817'). Not opened: Frankfurt Parliament page. REPAIR RUN (2026-11-01, German Confederation page re-read; Second Schleswig War and Province of Pomerania pages opened). (1) The earlier claim that the page does not list Austria's lands was wrong: the member table reads 'Austrian lands – Austria, Carinthia, Carniola and the Littoral except Istria' and 'Only included the Lands of the Bohemian Crown – Bohemia, Moravia and Austrian Silesia'. Every correction, the found region and the dissolve region now add Slovenia without Prekmurje and the Istrian coast (Pomurska, Koper, Izola and Piran subtracted; Pomurska also holds the Styrian Gornja Radgona and Ljutomer, an accepted error at the grid's scale), Gorizia and Trieste, and Trentino-South Tyrol. Tyrol south of the Brenner: the page contradicts itself (Italy section: 'autonomous region of Trentino-Alto Adige/Südtirol' inside the 1815-1866 boundaries; table footnote: the Confederation did not include 'upper Italian lands apart from Trieste'); I followed the Italy section and flag it here for a gap-filler. (2) Luxembourg: until 1839 the Grand Duchy also held today's Belgian province, drawn in keyframes 1815-1839 and in the 1815 gain; the 1839 loss to kingdom-of-belgium is a ledger event (year only: the page gives no month). (3) Auschwitz and Zator: the 1850 loss is added; the 1818-1850 circle is drawn in the 1820-1846 corrections (the Cliopatria year bands 1815-1819 and 1846-1852 cannot be split; the ledger dates are authoritative). (4) Federal execution in Holstein: occupation_start 1863-12 (24 December 1863, Second Schleswig War page) and occupation_end 1864-10 at confidence 1 (that page does not say when it ended; set to the Treaty of Vienna, as duchy-of-holstein does); Lauenburg is not named on either page, so Holstein only. (5) Thin items: Farther Pomerania (Słupsk, Lębork, Bytów) is added as a 50 km circle in every outline; the Province of Pomerania page does not mention the Confederation, so this rests on the Confederation page excluding only the Province of Prussia and the Grand Duchy of Posen from Prussia's membership (until 1848). Disagreement: the reviewer suggests dropping the 1866 contests against kingdom-of-prussia (ledger 11 and 12) in favour of the members' dossiers; I kept them because the Austro-Prussian War page names the Confederation itself as a belligerent against Prussia (the dossier's war entry), and a member-state contest is a different event; kingdom-of-prussia lacks the mirror contest, which is that batch's file.
